body_markdown:
Jonny Strickle, Group Managing Director of Pelagos Insurance Capital, recently sat down with Meg Green from Insurance Insider TV to discuss how Pelagos combines access, agility, and underwriting partnerships to allocate capital to the most attractive risk-adjusted opportunities.


During the conversation, Jonny Strickle shared his perspective on what differentiates Pelagos’ approach to capital allocation, what the company looks for in underwriting partners, and where he sees attractive opportunities for growth.


At the center of the conversation was Pelagos’ capital allocation strategy and the importance of having both the access and agility to deploy capital as market conditions evolve.


**On Pelagos’ approach to capital allocation:**


> Capital allocation for us is at the heart of everything that we do. \[…\] As we think about our capital allocation strategy, we think about risk-returns, the best areas of the market to go into, who’s the best partner… it’s about trying to get the right allocation of capital to the right risk through the right partner and at the right time.


**On the importance of access and agility to respond as pricing, terms, and broader conditions change:**


> “If you have a stale strategy, it stops being a winning one very, very quickly. \[…\] Having great access and having the confidence and ability to move the chips between different options at different times is really what’s key to our business model and what’s key to our success.”


**On selecting underwriting partnerships with expertise that complements and expands the opportunity set:**


> We want partners that are willing to work with us to shape the risk appetite to fit into our portfolio, that understand the agility we need to approach our capital allocation decisions with.


**On the opportunity ahead:**


> “In terms of growth opportunity right now, we still see attractive opportunity in most of the lines we write… we see lots of exciting opportunities, and that’s both with existing partners and with new partners.”
